safety.title: Safety guide
safety.description: Common scams in housing, jobs and second-hand deals, how to avoid them and where to report them.
safety.lead: Abroad, losses are much harder to recover. These few rules avoid most scams.

1.title: Don't send money before a viewing
1.body: A deposit, booking fee or “key delivery fee” asked up front is almost always a scam. Visit (or have someone you trust visit) and pay after signing the lease (bail).

2.title: Too cheap, too urgent
2.body: Rent far below market, “I'm abroad so I can't show it”, “you must decide today”: classic tricks.

3.title: Requests to move to another messenger
3.body: On KakaoTalk, Telegram or WhatsApp nothing is kept and reporting is hard. Keep talking in Itnyang chat.

4.title: Only the documents needed
4.body: Watermark passport or permit copies (“for rental application only”). Never give access to your bank account.

1.title: Avoid anyone charging you before you work
1.body: Training, uniform or registration fees up front mean a scam.

2.title: ID and bank details through an online form?
2.body: Some collect ID and bank details before any interview. Check that the business exists, with its address and contact, first.

3.title: Contract and payslip
3.body: In France, declared work (contract, payslip) is the rule. Pay below the minimum wage (SMIC) or cash only: think twice.

1.title: In person, in a public place
1.body: Check the item and pay somewhere busy, like a station or a café.

2.title: Prepayment “before I leave the country”
2.body: Many take a transfer (often to a Korean account) and vanish. Be extra careful with parcel deals.

1.title: Report on Itnyang
1.body: Use the “Report” button on a post, comment or chat. Moderators check and restrict the author. Keep your messages and payment records.

2.title: French police and online reporting
2.body: For online fraud, 17Cyber, the official police and gendarmerie site, assesses your case and explains how to report it. Report fraudulent or illegal content on PHAROS (internet-signalement.gouv.fr). If you lost money, file a complaint (plainte) at a police station (commissariat).

3.title: Emergency numbers
3.body: Police 17, European emergency number 112. If you can't speak, text 114.

4.title: Consular help from the embassy
4.body: Consular section of the Korean embassy in France: office hours (9:30–18:00) +33 1 47 53 01 01, after-hours emergencies +33 6 80 28 53 96. Consular call centre (Seoul, 24/7) +82 2 3210 0404. Scammers pose as the embassy, so call these numbers yourself to check.
